get.description: Returns a list of call events.

Retrieves an aggregated summary of call data based on the provided filters. This api is only available for accounts with Monitoring API feature.

The summary returned is broken down into time 'slices' depending on the time range requested.
The granularity is calculated based on:
 * 0-24 hours: hour
 * 25 hours - 7 days: day
 * 8 days - 30 days: week
 * 31+ days: month

Through the use of various query parameters, users can filter the call data by direction, phone numbers, sub-account, call result, SIP response codes, call type, hang-up source, and country.

Occasionally, underlying data may take longer than expected to load. To avoid connection timeouts, the API will return a `503 Service Unavailable` response in these cases, with an error message indicating that the data is still loading. If you receive a `503`, retry your request immediately with the exact same parameters.

Get a history of created reports.
Get the status of a report.
Get the file associated with a report.
Get a list of report definitions.

Lists the report definitions available to your account. A report definition is a template for a report you can run — it describes the report's category and domain, the filter parameters it accepts (with the operators and value types valid for each), the fields returned in each result row, and the execution flows it supports (`supportedModes`).

Use this endpoint to discover which reports you can run and to obtain each report's `reportDefinitionId`. Narrow the list with the `category`, `domain`, and `reportName` query parameters; results are paginated via `offset` and `limit`.

This is the starting point of the synchronous reporting workflow: list definitions here, fetch a single definition to inspect its filters in detail, then request its results.

This API currently supports the synchronous (`SYNC`) flow, so only report definitions that can be run synchronously are returned; definitions that use the asynchronous (`ASYNC`) flow are not available through this API.

This API is only available to accounts with access to the synchronous reports functionality.

Returns the full definition of a single report, identified by its `reportDefinitionId`. The response contains everything needed to run the report: its category and domain, the regions it covers, the maximum historical range available (`maxMonthsBack`), the complete list of filter parameters — with their supported operators, value types, and whether each is required — the output fields returned in each result row, and the execution flows it supports (`supportedModes`).

Call this after discovering a report via `GET /v2/report-definitions` to learn exactly how to construct a results request for it.

This API currently supports the synchronous (`SYNC`) flow, so a report definition that cannot be run synchronously is not retrievable through this endpoint.

This API is only available to accounts with access to the synchronous reports functionality.

post.description:
Runs the report identified by `reportDefinitionId` and returns its rows synchronously in the response — there is no job to poll and no file to download. The query criteria supplied in the request body are validated against the report's definition: at least one criterion is required, and some reports require specific parameters (for example a time range, or a `region` when the report spans more than one region).

Results are returned a page at a time — use `pageSize` and `pageNumber` to control paging, and follow the pagination links in the response to fetch subsequent pages.

Before calling this endpoint, use `GET /v2/report-definitions/{reportDefinitionId}` to discover the available filter parameters, operators, value types, and required fields, then pass matching criteria here.

Only report definitions that support the synchronous (`SYNC`) flow can be run through this endpoint. This API is only available to accounts with access to the synchronous reports functionality.

paginatedOperator.description:
Comparison operator applied to `values` against `parameter`.
  - `EQUAL` (`=`) — exact match; single value.
  - `GREATER` (`>`) — strictly greater than; single value.
  - `LESSER` (`<`) — strictly less than; single value.
  - `LESSER_OR_EQUAL` (`<=`) — less than or equal to; single value.
  - `GREATER_OR_EQUAL` (`>=`) — greater than or equal to; single value.
  - `LIKE` — SQL-style pattern match; single value.
  - `IN` — value matches any in the list; one or more values.
  - `CONTAINS` — substring match; single value.
  - `STARTS_WITH` — prefix match; single value.
  - `BETWEEN` — inclusive range; exactly two values `[lower, upper]`.

parameter.description:
Name of the parameter to filter on. Must match a `filterName` returned by
`GET /v2/report-definitions/{reportDefinitionId}`.

values.description:
Operand value(s) for the operator, always serialized as strings (the server
parses each value according to the parameter's declared type from the report
definition). Most operators take a single value; `IN` accepts one or more;
`BETWEEN` expects exactly two values `[lower, upper]`.

paginatedReportRequest.description:
Request body for generating report results. Query criteria target
parameters defined by the report definition; pagination is controlled via
`pageSize` and `pageNumber`.

queryCriteria.description:
List of criteria to apply to the report. At least one criterion is required;
individual reports may require specific parameters — call
`GET /v2/report-definitions/{reportDefinitionId}` to see which
parameters are marked `required: true` for that report.
When a report supports more than one region (see `regions` on the report
definition), a `region` criterion must also be supplied.

pageSize.description: Number of rows to return per page.

pageNumber.description: Zero-based index of the page to return.

validationType.description:
The validation rule applied to a filter value; a value that does not satisfy its rule is rejected with a 400.

- `E164`: a phone number in E.164 format, e.g. `"+12345678901"`.
- `REGEX`: a string matching the filter's own `validationRegex`, e.g. `"matchingValue"`.
- `ISO8601`: a full date-time with millisecond precision, e.g. `"2023-12-30T23:59:59.000Z"`.
- `ISO8601_RANGE`: a start and end date-time (millisecond precision), used with `BETWEEN`, e.g. `["2023-12-01T00:00:00.000Z", "2023-12-31T23:59:59.000Z"]`.
- `ISO8601_YEAR_MONTH`: a year and month, e.g. `"2023-12"`.
- `ISO8601_DATE`: a calendar date, e.g. `"2023-12-31"`.
- `STRING`: any string, e.g. `"someString"`.
- `INTEGER`: an integer, e.g. `123`.
- `ACCOUNT`: a customer account ID, e.g. `"9900000"`.

The `ISO8601*` types are also bounded by the report's `maxMonthsBack`.

monitorDirection.name: direction
monitorDirection.description:
Filter call data to only inbound or outbound calls.
If not provided, both inbound and outbound calls are returned in the results.

monitorTimestamp.name: timestamp
monitorTimestamp.description:
Timestamp range filter for the time range to return records for.
Use `gte` for the beginning of the range (defaults to '7 days ago' if not specified).
Use `lte` for the end of the range (defaults to 'now' if not specified).
Values should include timezone, else UTC will be assumed.
Note, results will only be returned going back up to one year.
A larger timespan, difference between `gte` and `lte` will make the results less granular, for example a timespan of a few days, results will be hourly, whilst a timespan of months, result will be monthly.

monitorFromPhoneNumber.name: fromPhoneNumber
monitorFromPhoneNumber.description:
Filter results by originating phone number(s) in E.164 format (e.g. `+353123456`).
Accepts a comma-separated list of numbers.
**Warning:** Using this parameter may result in dramatically slower responses.
To improve performance, use additional query parameters to reduce the scope of your query.

monitorToPhoneNumber.name: toPhoneNumber
monitorToPhoneNumber.description:
Filter results by destination phone number(s) in E.164 format (e.g. `+353123456`).
Accepts a comma-separated list of numbers.
**Warning:** Using this parameter may result in dramatically slower responses.
To improve performance, use additional query parameters to reduce the scope of your query.

monitorSubAccount.name: subAccount
monitorSubAccount.description:
Filter results by Sub-Account ID.
The user making this API call must have access to the specified sub-account.

monitorCallResult.name: callResult
monitorCallResult.description:
Filter results by call completion status.
Accepts a single value: `COMPLETED` or `INCOMPLETE`.
If not provided, results for all call results will be returned.

monitorResponseCode.name: responseCode
monitorResponseCode.description:
List of SIP response codes to filter for.
These are three digit codes, i.e. regex pattern `\d{3}`.
If not set, then all response codes are included.

monitorCallType.name: callType
monitorCallType.description:
Filter results by call type.
Accepts a single value: `NATIONAL`, `INTERNATIONAL`, `EMERGENCY` Etc.
If not provided, results for all call types will be returned.

monitorHangUpSource.name: hangUpSource
monitorHangUpSource.description:
Filter results by hang up source.
Accepts a single value: `CALLED_PARTY` or `CALLING_PARTY`.
If not provided, results for all hang up sources will be returned.

monitorSourceCountryCodeA3.name: sourceCountryCodeA3
monitorSourceCountryCodeA3.description:
Filter results by source country.
Accepts a comma-separated list of ISO A3 country codes (e.g. `USA`, `CAN`).
If not provided, results for all source countries will be returned.

monitorDestinationCountryCodeA3.name: destinationCountryCodeA3
monitorDestinationCountryCodeA3.description:
Filter results by destination country.
Accepts a comma-separated list of ISO A3 country codes (e.g. `USA`, `CAN`).
If not provided, results for all destination countries will be returned.

callIdPath.name: callId
callIdPath.description:
Filter Type: Exact Match, any valid call ID.

By default this is treated as a plain string. If the call ID contains characters that are not
permitted in a URL path (notably `/`), pass it as a base64url (RFC 4648 §5) encoded string and
set the `callIdEncoding` query parameter to `BASE64_URL` so it is decoded before lookup.

callIdEncoding.name: callIdEncoding
callIdEncoding.description:
Opt-in encoding applied to the `callId` path parameter. When set to `BASE64_URL`, the
`callId` is decoded as a base64url (RFC 4648 §5) string before lookup. This allows call IDs
containing characters that are not permitted in a URL path (notably `/`) to be passed safely.

When omitted or set to `RAW`, the `callId` is used verbatim. Standard Base64 is not supported because its
`+` and `/` characters would reintroduce the path-encoding problem.

Note: If no startTime or endTime is specified, startTime will default to the last 24 hours.

callingNumber.name: callingNumber
callingNumber.description:
Short number exact match, Short number Multimatch, Short number prefix match, E.164 exact match, E.164 Multimatch, E.164 prefix match, Alphanumeric exact match, Alphanumeric Multimatch, Alphanumeric prefix match.

Example:

* Short number exact match: 15555551234

* Short number Multimatch: 1555*,1234*,15555551234,15555554567

* Short number prefix match: 1555*

* E.164 exact match: +15555551234

* E.164 Multimatch: +1555*,+1234*,+15555551234,+15555554567

* E.164 prefix match: +1555*

* Alphanumeric exact match: WO1234567

* Alphanumeric Multimatch: WO1234567, PO4567891, WO*, PO*

* Alphanumeric prefix match: WO*

Alphanumeric string of length 1 to 15 characters with optional leading '+' (URL encoded as %2B) and optional trailing '*' (indicating prefix search)

Alphanumeric string of length 1 to 15 characters with optional leading '+' (URL encoded as %2B) and optional trailing '*' (indicating prefix search)

Basic.description:
Basic authentication is a simple authentication scheme built into the HTTP protocol. To use it, send your HTTP requests with an `Authorization` header that contains the word `Basic` followed by a space and a Base64-encoded string `username:password`.

- Example: `Authorization: Basic ZGVtbZpwQDU1dzByZA==`

Bearer.description:
Bearer authentication (also called token authentication) is an HTTP authentication scheme that involves security tokens called bearer tokens. The name “Bearer authentication” can be understood as “give access to the bearer of this token.” The client must send this token in the `Authorization` header when making requests to protected resources.

- Example: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

Where `<token>` should be replaced with the token string without angle brackets.

For more information, see the following guide: [Credentials](https://dev.bandwidth.com/docs/account/credentials/management)
